original.description: Survivors of the Japanese carrier Hiryu — her engineering force, taken from an open boat on 19 June 1942 after two weeks adrift — sitting on mats on the deck of USS Ballard (AVD-10). Official U.S. Navy photograph 80-G-79974-1.
original.photographer: U.S. Navy (photographer not named in the Online Library record)
original.archive: Official U.S. Navy photograph 80-G-79974-1, now in the collections of the National Archives; Naval Historical Center Online Library, read via the ibiblio.org HyperWar mirror
original.original_dimensions: 740 × 510 (Online Library scan; the printed caption strip along the bottom edge is cropped here, and nothing else is altered)
original.licence: public domain — official U.S. Navy photograph, a work of the United States federal government (80-G series, National Archives)

colorization.status: not colorized, and this one should stay so: these are prisoners of war, photographed exhausted, and the project publishes the record itself rather than a treatment of it

content_policy: ok — living prisoners of war, exhausted but unwounded; no gore. Published as the Navy's own record of the rescue, with the men's circumstances stated plainly in the caption
caption: Survivors of Hiryū on the deck of USS Ballard, June 1942 — the engineering force left aboard when the carrier was abandoned on 5 June, taken from an open boat on the 19th after two weeks adrift. Jay Tashner's service record credits him with participating in their capture. Official U.S. Navy photograph 80-G-79974-1.
credit: Official U.S. Navy photograph 80-G-79974-1, now in the collections of the National Archives; via the Naval Historical Center Online Library (ibiblio.org mirror). Public domain.
notes: Fetched 2026-08-30 from the Online Library page catalogued in source:nhc-midway-rescue, which quotes the rescue account in full. The scan carries the Library's printed caption strip along the bottom edge; the strip is cropped and nothing else is altered. A higher-resolution master exists at the National Archives under 80-G-79974 for whoever fetches it for the Midway pack (sand-lry.6).
